goal: Maximize tcp_goodput_bps subject to udp_loss_frac <= 0.01, treating differences below the 1% tolerance as equal.
limit: The result is limited by the fixed UDP offered load and the 1 Gbps link: UDP consumes about 307 Mbps of wire capacity, leaving about 668.6 Mbps payload for TCP when the link is saturated. Any TCP gain requires UDP drops; the 1% UDP loss cap allows only a 0.35% TCP gain over default. Evidence E1, E2, E3.
explanation: The scheduler is work-conserving: when UDP demand is below its configured share, TCP uses the unused UDP share, so TCP goodput is flat for weightUdp values from 0.31 to 0.5 (E1). The UDP demand threshold is about 0.307; below that, UDP drops appear and TCP gains capacity, but the udp_loss_frac<=0.01 constraint stops the gain at weightUdp about 0.304, which is only 0.35% above the default (E2, E3). Since that gain is inside the 1% tolerance, the simplest default settings are recommended. tcpVariant matters only because BBR and Vegas underutilize the link; loss-based variants are equal (E2). queuePkts=1000 hurts TCP by more than 1%, while 4/10/100 are equal at a safe weight (E2, E3). duration has no meaningful effect (E3).
holds_when: UDP offered load remains 300 Mbps, the scheduler is work-conserving, the link is saturated, queue sizes are not huge, and a loss-based TCP variant is used.
breaks_when: If the UDP loss tolerance were larger, lower weightUdp values would be better; if the scheduler were not work-conserving, weightUdp would directly limit TCP; if UDP rate changes, the safe weight threshold changes; BBR/Vegas or very large queues would reduce TCP goodput.

claims.text: Default settings satisfy udp_loss_frac<=0.01 and give tcp_goodput_bps=668633114.
The scheduler is work-conserving: TCP goodput is unchanged for weightUdp=0.31 through 0.5.
Lowering weightUdp below the UDP demand threshold increases TCP only by dropping UDP; the best feasible tested gain is 0.35%, inside tolerance.
BBR and Vegas underutilize the link, while loss-based variants are equal within tolerance.
queuePkts=1000 lowers TCP by more than 1%; 4/10/100 are equal at a safe weight.
duration does not change the measured result.

open_questions: The exact weightUdp threshold for udp_loss_frac=0.01 lies between 0.303 and 0.304 but was not narrowed further.
The large-queue anomaly in r030 (zero drops but reduced UDP goodput) was not fully traced.
Seed sensitivity was not tested because seed is fixed by the system.
